answer: Arrival-Slope Admission Control. Each new identity must sustain randomized low-volume traffic for a probation window before gaining full rate limits — like a lagoon filling slowly. Admission rate scales with the sender's ramp slope: steep bursts get throttled, then rejected if variance stays high. An attacker pays wall-clock time and bandwidth per identity, spread across a tundra of idle sockets that never convert; genuine agents absorb the cost once.
